science: Plants need light and water to grow.
Space gardens use special red and blue lights, which make the garden glow pink and purple.
Seeds grow in small plant pillows; water floats in wobbly balls in space, so watering is done carefully.
Leaves grow toward the light. Lettuce takes weeks to grow.
Real astronauts have grown and eaten lettuce, and grown zinnia flowers, on the space station.
parent.summary: The crew plants seeds in the station's glowing garden. Then comes the hard part: waiting.

options: Lettuce: the ending is a big, crunchy bite.
Zinnias: the ending is a bright orange flower for Button.

paths.moment: Dig up a seed to peek, or let the seeds rest
options: Peek: the little root droops out of its pillow. The crew tucks it back in, says sorry, and lets it rest. Later it grows strong.
Rest: the seeds grow quietly, hidden in their pillows.
Draw a picture of the garden (Button draws a very square circle).
Sing a growing song to the plants.

talk: What is something that's hard to wait for?
What can we do to help the waiting go by?
What do plants need to grow?

beats.say: In a cozy corner of Star Station, there is a tiny garden.
It glows pink and purple, like a sunset in a box.
"Why is it pink?" asked {a}.
"Plants need light to grow," said Button. "Our garden has special red lights and blue lights. Together, they make our garden glow pink and purple!"
"And plants need water, too. Light and water help plants grow."
{T}, can you turn on the garden lights? Tap anywhere!
"Real astronauts have grown lettuce in space," said Button. "And they ate it, too!"

choice.say: {A}, what should we grow in our space garden?

options.label: Flowers
options.say: Or bright orange flowers, called zinnias?

beats.say: Lettuce it is! Crunch, crunch!
Zinnias it is! Real astronauts have grown zinnia flowers in space, too.
In space, seeds grow in little plant pillows. Soft and puffy, and filled with special soil.
{T}, can you tuck the seeds into their pillows? Tap each pillow!
One, two, three. All tucked in. Sleep tight, little seeds.
Now the seeds need a drink.
Button gave the water pouch a gentle squeeze. Out came a wobbly, wiggly ball of water!
"In space, water floats in wobbly little balls," said Button. "So we water our plants very, very carefully."
{A}, can you help? Tap the water pouch. Gently, three times.
Blup. Blup. Blup. A drink for every seed.
And now... we wait.
{t} looked at the pillows. Nothing. Not one tiny leaf.
{t} looked again. Still nothing.
"Grow, seeds! Grow!" said {t}.
"Seeds take time," said Button. "Lots and lots of time."
{T}, can you give the seeds a little wave? Tap anywhere!
Waiting is hard. It's very, very hard.

options.label: Peek
options.say: Dig up a seed, and take a peek?

options.label: Wait
options.say: Or let the seeds rest, and wait?

beats.say: {crew} dug gently into one pillow, to take a peek.
And there was the seed! It had a teeny, tiny root, as thin as a hair. It was just starting to grow.
But out of its cozy pillow, the little root began to droop.
"Oh dear," said Button softly. "Little roots like to stay tucked in."
So, gently, gently, {crew} tucked the seed back into its pillow.
"Sorry, little seed," whispered {a}. "[We'll|I'll] let you rest now."
{T}, can you give it a soft little pat? Tap anywhere.
{crew} let the seeds rest in their cozy pillows.
And deep inside, where no one could see, the seeds were busy.
Tiny roots were starting to grow. Down, down, down.
But what can we do while we wait?
{T}, can you make some floaty bubbles while we think? Tap anywhere!

options.label: Draw
options.say: Draw a picture of our garden?

options.label: Sing
options.say: Or sing a growing song to the plants?

beats.say: [{a} drew tall green leaves, and {t} drew a big, round sun with a happy face.|{a} drew tall green leaves, under a big, round, smiling sun.]
Button drew... a very square circle. "Robots are still learning to draw," said Button.
Grow, grow, little seed. Here's the light and drink you need!
Button hummed along. Hmmm, beep. Hmmm, boop.
And then, the days went by.
{T}, can you help the days go by? Every time you tap, we'll sleep and wake up again!
Lots and lots of sleeps went by. Weeks and weeks.
Then, one morning, {t} floated into the garden, and gasped.
"Look!" Poking out of a pillow was a teeny, tiny, curly green sprout.
{T}, can you say hello to the sprout? Tap it, very gently.
"Hello, sprout," whispered Button. "Welcome to Star Station."
Every day, the crew gave the plants a little drink. And every day, the plants grew a tiny bit more.
And look! Little green plants, reaching up toward the lights.
"See how the leaves grow toward the light?" said Button. "In space, light helps plants know which way to grow."
Even the little seed that took a peek was growing. Slow, and strong.
The lettuce grew big, crinkly leaves.
The zinnias opened bright orange petals, like tiny suns.
{T}, can you give the garden a big hello? Tap anywhere!
At last, the lettuce was ready. {crew} took a big bite. Crunch!
Button couldn't eat lettuce. Robots don't. But Button loved the crunchy sound. "Again!" beeped Button.
At last, the zinnias were in full bloom. {a} picked one, and gave it to Button.
Button tucked the flower behind its antenna. "How do I look?" "Beautiful!"
A message crackled in from Mission Control, far below on the Earth. "Beautiful garden, Star Station!"
And in its cozy corner, the little garden glowed pink and purple, growing a tiny bit more every day.
